1.title: Understand freight and storage markets
1.intro: Goods move by road, rail, air and sea; storage buffers timing.
pts: Map one route: origin, mode, handover, destination, with times.
Know cost drivers: distance, weight, speed, handling, empty returns.
Study cold chain and dangerous goods as special cases.
Choose a niche: local last-mile, cold storage, small-parcel consolidation.
Learn each mode's strength: road for flexibility, rail for heavy bulk over distance, air for speed, sea for volume; write one example for each.
Note seasonal swings such as harvest, holiday peaks and spring road limits; check the provincial weight rule.
Interview three shippers about volume, timing and damage history.
1.ex: A shipper sends 12 pallets weekly to three towns. If a loaded trip costs 100 per pallet and empty returns add 30%, the cost is 130 per pallet. Over 12 pallets that is 1,560 instead of 1,200, a difference of 360 a week.

2.title: Know transport and safety rules
pts: Commercial driver licensing, hours-of-service and vehicle inspections apply.
Dangerous goods need training and documents.
Food and medicine storage need temperature records.
Cross-border rules need customs paperwork.
Learn that axle weights and spring road limits are set by the province; check the provincial rule before you plan a load.
Write a daily pre-trip inspection checklist and keep signed copies.
Check insurance requirements for carriers and warehouse operators; check the provincial and federal rule.
2.ex: Row: 'Drive commercial truck | provincial and federal transport rules | licence, logs, inspection | each day | log book'. A second row: 'Store chilled food | food safety rule | temperature log against the limit in the rule | at the interval the rule sets; check it | log sheet'. Date each source.

3.title: Plan routes and warehouse flow
3.intro: Good plans save kilometres and handling.
pts: Group stops by area and time window.
Load in reverse stop order.
Warehouse flow: receive, check, put-away, pick, pack, ship.
Use simple software.
Order stops by time window first, then by distance.
Design the dock with separate receiving and shipping areas where possible and keep aisles clear.
Count touches: every extra handling adds cost and damage risk, so cut one.
3.ex: Route A: 22 stops in 188 km versus 241 km unplanned. The saving is 53 km, which is 53 / 241 = 22%. At 1.20 per km for fuel and wear that is 63.60 saved per route.

4.title: Cost per load and per pallet position
pts: Vehicle cost per km, driver cost per hour, fuel, insurance.
Warehouse cost per pallet per month.
Utilisation: loaded share of capacity.
Margin and break-even.
Work out vehicle cost per km: fuel, tires, repairs, depreciation and insurance divided by km driven.
For the warehouse, divide rent, utilities and labour by pallet positions to get cost per position per month.
Test a utilisation case: if loads run 70% full, revenue per trip falls.
4.ex: Load price 2,400; cost 1,800; margin 600 (25%); fixed cost 24,000 a month gives 24,000 / 600 = 40 loads. At 70% utilisation revenue is 2,400 x 0.7 = 1,680 against the same 1,800 cost, a loss of 120 per load. Teaching figures in CAD.
4.act: Build a cost sheet with 70% utilisation case.

5.title: Run on time and damage-free
pts: Track on-time and damage rates.
Inspect and photograph loads.
Preventive maintenance.
Handle claims fast.
Record arrival time at each stop against the promised window.
Photograph the load at pickup and at delivery and get a signed receipt.
Schedule maintenance by kilometres and log it; a missed service goes in the risk register.
5.ex: On-time 94%: 47 of 50 deliveries arrived in the window. Damage 0.8%: 4 pallets of 500 were damaged. Track both every week and set a target for next month.

6.title: Win shippers and partners
pts: Offer trial loads.
Quote in writing with terms.
Partner with brokers and warehouses.
Track funnel.
Write a one-page rate card with minimum charge, waiting time and cancellation terms.
Offer a trial of five loads at the normal price, judged against an agreed on-time target.
Ask partner brokers for one thing to improve and record the answer.
6.ex: Funnel: 25 shippers, 8 quotes, 3 customers. Quote rate is 8 / 25 = 32%, win rate is 3 / 8 = 37.5%, and overall 3 / 25 = 12%. To win six customers you would contact about 50 shippers.

7.title: Manage safety, weather and cargo risk
pts: Fatigue and speed controls.
Winter driving plans.
Cargo insurance.
Theft prevention.
Set a rule for when a driver must stop for rest or bad weather, and state that no one is penalised for stopping.
Prepare a winter kit and check the provincial rule on tires and chains.
Compare cargo insurance limits with the value of a pallet.
7.ex: Risk: 'Winter delay | 4 x 3 | buffer days and alerts | dispatcher | each season'. The score is 4 x 3 = 12. If a lost pallet is worth 6,000 and cover is 5,000, 1,000 is uninsured.

8.title: Pilot a lane
pts: 60 days.
Measure on-time, cost per pallet.
Stop rule: margin under 10% means re-price.
Plan growth.
Choose a lane with a willing shipper and repeat loads, such as two a week.
Record cost per pallet and on-time rate every week.
Decide in writing on day 60 whether to continue, re-price or stop.
8.ex: Margin 22%: at a price of 2,400 the cost is 2,400 x 0.78 = 1,872 and the margin is 528. That is above the 10% stop line (240), so proceed and plan growth.

quiz: Share of vehicle or space used.
Deliveries on time divided by all.
